t.sf12827dd43: In the morning the sun comes up, in the day it shines bright, in the evening it goes down, at night the moon comes out! Show a move for each one!
t.s455d701c5b: In the morning — stretch, at night — rest your head.
t.s7f645c8d00: Switch the light on and off and play day and night.
t.s4a0fee3768: The sun is setting. When is that?
t.s25c25b263c: When do the moon and stars come out?
t.s7c91f60b6a: What do we do at night?
t.s24e3fd8c6a: That's right! At night we sleep.
t.sa78b5e67dd: Beep-beep! The parts of the day lined up, but they got mixed up. Who is first, who is last? Let's put them in order!
t.s1f0aa50a0e: First comes morning, then daytime, then evening, and at the end night. Then morning comes again. The day goes round and round!
t.s40dba5e15f: First we eat breakfast, then we go to kindergarten. First we brush our teeth, then we go to sleep. Order matters!
t.s8dd0a68530: Act out your day: waking up, breakfast, play, dinner, sleep! Let your family guess what time it is!
t.s704f682379: Draw the parts of the day on paper and put them in order.
t.sa66cd727f2: Well done! After morning comes daytime.
t.s7f5a300aec: Great job! After evening comes night.
t.s304474194d: That's right! First teeth, then sleep.
t.s3b6b96c6c0: 🌅☀️🌇🌙 — how many parts does the day have?
t.s042e617155: Awesome! Four parts of the day.
t.s7e43bcbafe: Beep-beep! Two little birds were sitting on a branch. Then one more flew in — that was me! How many of us are there now?
t.s14df16880b: There were two little birds. One more joined them. When we add, we get more! Now let's count: one, two, three.
t.scc3c7eceb3: Let's count the old ones and the new one together: one, two, three. Three little birds in all!
t.s5b06af92da: Take two blocks in your hand. Ask Mom to give you one more. How many now? Count! Add one more — how many now?
t.s8db6ff7790: Add one more block to one block.
t.s374757fd8b: On your fingers: two fingers and one more — how many?
t.s7dae38f73e: 🐟🐟 were there, then 🐟 joined. How many now?
t.s8f1886e473: Well done! Two and one make three.
t.sbe97950902: 🍎🍎🍎 were there, then one more 🍎 came. How many?
t.sba672c4a3e: Great job! Three and one make four.
t.s8a83092b85: What happens to things when more are added?
t.sd8fac36686: That's right! When we add, there are more.
t.sfb21096e42: Beep-beep! Three frogs were sitting by the pond. One jumped into the water — splash! How many are left?
t.s3b0e7afdc5: There were three frogs. One went away. When someone leaves, there are fewer! Now let's count the ones that are left.
t.se0135d464d: We don't count the one that left, only the ones still here: one, two. Two frogs are left!
t.s71f31424d6: 🐸🐸🐸 were there, one went away. How many are left?
t.s9e81670104: Well done! Three, one went away — two are left.
t.s161c05614c: 🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈 were there, one flew away. How many are left?
t.s00b91d0193: Great job! Five, one flew away — four are left.
t.s67a0982728: What happens to things when some go away?
t.s1410b3f3e4: That's right! When some go away, there are fewer.
t.se1163f787e: 🐦🐦 were there, then 🐦🐦 more came. How many?
t.se3b47f5078: Awesome! Two and two make four.
t.s8e146d8c86: Beep-beep! I'm going to tell you little stories. Listen carefully: did someone come or go away? Then we'll count!
t.sc65ca7957c: If the story says «came, gave, joined» — there are more. If it says «went away, ate, flew away» — there are fewer. Let's listen to the words!
t.s49cb2248e5: Hold up three fingers, fold two down!
t.sdc992dfad1: There were three apples — we hold up three fingers. We ate two — we fold two fingers down. One is left!
t.sf5eed90749: Tell a story with your toys: «Three little bears were playing. One went home.» How many are left? Now make up your own story!
t.sda9c383b05: Two toys, one more came — how many?
t.sf9abb5c4bd: Tell your family a story problem and let them solve it.
t.s9b5278a1c4: Ali had 2 toy cars. His dad gave him 2 more. How many does he have now?
t.s1d46874c06: Well done! Two and two make four.
t.sb3c1737ee3: There were 4 cookies on the plate. Zebo ate one. How many are left?
t.s826ad56880: Great job! Four take away one is three.
t.s97a0451adb: «A puppy came running.» What happened to the puppies?
t.s7722944248: That's right! One came — there are more.
t.s1253dd392b: There were 5 chicks in the nest. 2 ran away. How many are left?
t.s28f8376589: Awesome! Five, two ran away — three are left.
t.s1e8d9992c4: Beep-beep! I have five apples. I'll put them into two baskets. Can we do it in different ways? Let's try!
t.s1aeace4642: We put five apples into two baskets: two in one, three in the other. Count them together — five again! One and four also make five.
t.sf55eb2445a: There were two apples in the basket. We ate them both. They're all gone — the basket is empty, nothing is left!
t.sef69c1576d: Hold up five fingers. Fold two down — how many are still up? Three! Now fold them all down — nothing is left! You made a fist!
t.s42f00f8f4d: Fold down one finger out of five.
t.sb8a2813730: Split five blocks between your two hands in different ways and count.
t.sbb66a6295e: Well done! Two and three make five.
t.seb786cd84e: 🍬🍬🍬 were there, and we ate them all. What is left?
t.s7f6ac076da: Great job! They're all gone — nothing is left.
t.sd943d057b6: That's right! One and four make five.
t.s3d2475ae56: Awesome! Five is more than three.
t.sbc0b06cc93: Hello, my friend! I'm robot Kabu. Beep-beep! Today we're going on a trip to Number Land. There, every number is a living hero! Two friends are waiting for us first. Who could they be?
t.sf0c1d2ca28: This is the number zero. Look, it looks like a round egg 🥚! When there isn't a single apple left in the basket, we say «zero» — there's nothing. Draw a big circle in the air with your finger — there's zero!
t.s3f5ba4affd: This is the number one. It looks like a soldier standing tall: straight, thin, with a little nose at the top 📏. One sun ☀️, one nose 👃 — they're all one! Hold one finger straight up and show me.
t.s7b3348528b: Let's sing together! «Zero is a little egg, round and empty through. One's a little soldier, standing tall, nose up too!» Now when we say zero, make a circle with your arms, and on one, stand up tall!
t.sdc3d6f2926: There's nothing in the basket 🧺. How many apples are there?
t.s3937ba12c9: That's right! Nothing there — that's zero.
t.sb25f0b4654: How many suns are in the sky? ☀️
t.sf58009170e: Well done! There's one sun — one.
t.s7ae32be896: Which number looks like a round egg? 🥚
t.sb82afdd0a1: Great job! Zero is round like an egg.
t.s0495aa8a06: Which number looks like a soldier standing tall? 💂
t.s2de684aa15: Super! One is a straight soldier standing tall.
t.s64445207e8: Beep-beep! Yesterday we met zero and one. Today two guests are swimming on the lake in Number Land. One is a swan — and what does the other look like? Let's see!
t.s02f12016bc: This is the number two. It looks like a swan swimming on the lake 🦢: a curved neck at the top and a flat tummy at the bottom. We have two eyes 👀 and two hands. Show me two fingers!
t.s642d01894a: This is the number three. Look, from the side it looks like a snowman with two round tummies ⛄ — one half circle on top, another one below. A traffic light has three lights 🚦: red, yellow, green. Show me three fingers!
t.sc4c75fd697: When I say «two», spread your arms like wings and swim like a swan. When I say «three», make yourself round like a snowman. When I say «one», stand tall like a soldier! Ready? Two! Three! One! Three! Well done!
t.s2f57de3eaf: A swan is swimming on the lake 🦢. Which number looks like a swan?
t.s3de7094515: That's right! Two is a little swan.
t.s96327538e9: How many lights does a traffic light have? 🚦
t.s7fc68dcd87: Well done! Red, yellow, green — three.
t.s0957622986: Great job! We have two eyes.
t.sedbb91abfc: Super! One, two, three — three balloons.
t.s50431de187: Beep-beep! There's a little house in Number Land. In front of it lies an upside-down chair, and by the door stands a round-bellied boy in a hat. They are the numbers four and five! Let's meet them.
t.sbbaf597fca: This is the number four. It looks like an upside-down chair with its legs in the air 🪑. A cat has four legs 🐈, and a table has four legs too. Show me four fingers!
t.s1f69c98fae: This is the number five. It looks like a boy with a round tummy wearing a flat hat 🎩. We have five fingers on one hand ✋. Open your hand and count: one, two, three, four, five!
t.s02c9eeda8a: Raise your hand and fold each finger as you sing: «One — the thumb, two — the pointer, three — the middle, four — the ring finger, five — the little pinky! Five little fingers make one hand, let's clap along, oh, isn't it grand!» Now clap: one, two, three, four, five!
t.sd0a93b40c8: How many legs does a cat have? 🐈
t.s1bc5fd6995: That's right! A cat has four legs.
t.sf2dfd86369: How many fingers are on one hand? ✋
t.sf4aff96629: Which number looks like an upside-down chair? 🪑
t.se3bf5b64af: Great job! Four is an upside-down chair.
t.s6c470a6ab1: Beep-beep! Zero, one, two, three, four, five — they've all gathered! They're standing in a line. But there's a secret: to count correctly, there's a special rule. What is it? Let's find out!
t.seb7cb05258: When we count, we point at each thing with a finger just once 👉. We don't skip any, and we don't count anything twice. The last number we say tells us how many there are in all. For example: 🍎🍎🍎 — one, two, three. Three apples!
t.s8ff78b3412: Numbers always line up in the same order: zero, one, two, three, four, five. Each next number is one more. March and count: one number for each step!
t.sb8745272dc: I say a number, and you clap that many times! Three — 👏👏👏. Four! One! Five! Zero — no clapping at all, we stand still! Awesome, you're a real counting champ!
t.s3e4682fcb8: That's right! One, two, three, four — four fish.
t.s8cb5c22e65: Which number comes after 2 in the row?
t.s3d4b1e08d9: Great job! One, two, three — 3 comes after 2.
t.sf41e03c287: Beep-beep! There's a garden in Number Land. A snail is crawling through it, and next to it stands a bent lamppost. Guess what — they're numbers too! Who are they?
t.s31563da318: Show five fingers and one more!
t.s3e113d8c80: This is the number six. It looks like a snail 🐌: a round shell at the bottom, and its head stretched up high. Five fingers and one more make six. Look: ✋☝️ — six!
t.sd6284812e9: This is the number seven. It looks like a street lamp bending its head 🏮: a line across the top and a slanted post going down. A rainbow has seven colors 🌈. And a week has seven days too!
t.sdbe5e06d03: When I say «six», crouch down like a snail and lift your head. When I say «seven», stand tall like a lamp and bend your head. Six! Seven! Six! Now let's count slowly: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven — and clap!
t.scac7e7e7cb: Which number looks like a snail? 🐌
t.s55d9ab48ac: That's right! Six is a little snail.
t.sc40f67f3e2: How many colors does a rainbow have? 🌈
t.s0016c0d191: Well done! A rainbow has seven colors.
t.sb52ecfa256: Which number looks like a bent lamppost? 🏮
t.sb7ce33e9f7: Super! Seven is a bent lamp.
t.s7507075770: Beep-beep! Winter has come, and snow fell in Number Land. The children made a snowman out of two round snowballs. Next to it, a balloon on a string is floating. These are eight and nine!
t.sfbdaec06bb: Draw an eight in the air!
t.s6faae34e39: This is the number eight. It looks like a snowman made of two round snowballs ⛄: a small loop on top, a big loop at the bottom. An octopus has eight arms 🐙. Draw an eight in the air — keep going without stopping!
t.s55c342f518: This is the number nine. It looks like a balloon on a string 🎈: a round balloon on top, with the string hanging down. If we turn six upside down, we get nine! Six has its circle at the bottom, like a snail, and nine has its circle on top.
t.s3996597800: Write the number 6 on paper and turn it upside down — what do you get? Nine! The snail turned into a balloon. Remember: circle at the bottom — six, circle on top — nine.
t.s9381418a25: Which number looks like a snowman? ⛄
t.s7a5d0b0c20: That's right! Eight is two snowballs.
t.s39eb7fa90a: How many arms does an octopus have? 🐙
t.sa38b2f7a36: Which number has its circle on top and its string at the bottom? 🎈
t.s4deedd5444: Great job! Nine is a balloon on a string.
t.s757afb5cb9: Beep-beep! It's a party in Number Land! One and zero held hands and stood side by side — and a new number appeared. What number is it? Let's find out with our fingers!
t.s9aa03dd6bb: This is the number ten. It has two digits: first one, then zero 1️⃣0️⃣. The little soldier and the little egg stood side by side and made ten! We have ten fingers on our two hands in all 🙌.
t.s825d6e5c8c: Now we can count to ten: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten! Each number is one more than the one before. Open your fingers one at a time and count.
t.s94cb5163aa: Let's sing and open our fingers one by one: «One, two — hands up high, three, four — clap, clap, clap, five, six — jump once, seven, eight — spin around, nine, ten — take a bow, we can count so well now!»
t.s57838fe15d: How many fingers are on two hands? 🙌
t.sae37faca8d: That's right! Two hands have ten fingers.
t.se73a50adee: Which digits make the number ten?
t.sde7c006c48: Well done! First one, then zero — ten.
t.sae10e7cc99: Beep-beep! Two squirrels were gathering nuts. The first one says: «I have more!» The second one says: «No, I have more!» Who is right? Let's count and help them make up.
t.sc6c17311a3: Let's count two groups. The group with the bigger number has more. 🍎🍎🍎🍎🍎 — five, 🍎🍎 — two. Five is bigger than two, so the first basket has more!
t.seada1bfa6c: The group with the smaller number has fewer. 🐤🐤🐤 — three, 🐤 — one. One is less than three, so where there's one chick, there are fewer.
t.sfe4963ff10: If two groups have the same number, they are equal. 🍪🍪🍪 and 🍪🍪🍪 — three and three. Nobody has more or fewer — they're equal! Now the squirrels can make up.
t.s8b83638c06: That's right! Four is more than two.
t.sfc20dc2bd2: Well done! Three is less than five.
t.s018cf068a6: Great job! Three and three — they're equal.
t.s1bb9678555: One squirrel 🐿️ gathered 7 nuts, the other 🐿️ gathered 9. Who has more?
t.scc9db34d0d: Super! Nine is more than seven.
t.s3a3dbfa5be: Beep-beep! Today we're going to be astronauts! Our rocket is ready to fly. But for the rocket to take off, we need to count backwards. How do we do that? Buckle up!
t.s139d9db6f2: Squat down a little on each number!
t.sfd7f487a4a: Usually we count forward: one, two, three. When we count backwards, we start from a big number and take away one each time: five, four, three, two, one. Just like walking down the stairs 🪜!
t.s8b87507e4f: Counting backwards ends when we reach zero. The rocket says: five, four, three, two, one, zero — blast off! 🚀 Zero is the smallest number, we don't go below it.
t.s7a0aff96b1: Crouch down — you're a rocket! Count backwards with me and rise a little on each number: five, four, three, two, one... ZERO! Jump and stretch your arms up high — blast off! 🚀 One more time!
t.s333becdfbd: Let's count backwards: 5, 4, 3, ... What comes next?
t.s663ef407fd: That's right! Five, four, three, two.
t.sba94f14983: On which number does the rocket take off? 🚀
t.s5e7c166994: Well done! On zero — blast off!
t.s37f8481853: When we count backwards, what number comes after 3?
t.s3d3936b04b: At which number does counting backwards end?
t.sa7a49131ce: Super! Counting backwards ends at zero.
t.s816f03a36f: Beep-beep! Yesterday's rocket was small. Today we have a big rocket — it's flying to a faraway planet! For it, we need to count backwards from ten, not from five. Ready, astronauts?
t.s3039468092: Bend your fingers one by one!
t.sa50cd2ce9b: Now let's start from ten: ten, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two, one, zero! With each step the number gets one smaller. Count and bend your fingers one by one 🙌.
t.s4d74b93bf9: When we count backwards, each number is one less than the one before. There are 🍪🍪🍪🍪 four cookies on the plate. If we eat one — three are left. Backwards after four comes — three!
t.s0284f62c23: «Ten little sparrows sat on a tree, one flew away — whoosh! Now there are nine, you see...» Each time one flies away: eight, seven, six... and at the end zero — the branch is empty! Make wings with your arms and flap them on every «whoosh».
t.s2cd786bbd3: That's right! Ten, nine, eight, seven.
t.see1485f732: Counting backwards, which number comes after 6?
t.s981899667c: 🍪🍪🍪🍪🍪 five cookies. We ate one. How many are left?
t.sf76f20fa34: Great job! One less than five is four.
t.s1e20ddd028: Which number did we start counting backwards from?
t.s7e1f87609e: Super! Today we started from ten.
t.s47230d5947: Beep-beep! On Number Street the houses stand in a row. Every number has two neighbours: one lives on the left, one on the right. Let's go and meet them!
t.s9b513581a4: The next number is the one that comes right after when you count. It is one more. The number after 4 is — 5, because four, then five. If one more chick comes to 🐤🐤🐤🐤 — there will be five!
t.s229f0f6ec8: The number before is the one that comes earlier when you count. It is one less. The number before 4 is — 3. Remember counting backwards: four, then three!
t.sd3cdfd7f8c: Every number has two neighbours: the one before and the one after. The neighbours of 5 are — 4 and 6. Zero has only one neighbour — 1, because there is no number smaller than zero.
t.sb70c203e1a: I say a number — you say its neighbours! Raise your left hand and say the one before, raise your right hand and say the one after. Five! — Four and six! Two! — One and three! Eight! — Seven and nine! Well done!
t.s0c3f3abb5a: Well done! Seven, then eight — so the number before is seven.
t.s63962d228e: Great job! Two and four are the neighbours of three.
t.s8eadc83c8a: Beep-beep! Oh no, the wind blew and one number flew out of the row! Now there is an empty spot. Who can help? The neighbours will show us the way!
t.s85d45a755e: Look at the row: 1, 2, ❓, 4. The empty spot is between two and four. After two comes — three! So the missing number is — 3.
t.s713f52c5b0: If there is one spot between two numbers, the middle number lives there. Between 6 and 8 is — 7. Count to check: six, seven, eight. Right!
t.s87b95353fc: That's right! Between four and six is five.
t.sf6df9c313d: Backwards row: 5, ❓, 3, 2. Which number is missing?
t.sb245542fcf: Row: ❓, 1, 2, 3. Which number is at the very start?
t.s33e4c356e1: Super! The number before one is zero.
t.sa25e7e237e: Beep-beep! Every number has a little two-room house. In the left room live some guests, in the right room live the rest. All together — that's the number! Let's put the guests into the houses.
t.s056629d683: Let's split three balloons into two rooms: one on the left 🔴, two on the right 🔴🔴. One and two — together three! So 3 is 1 and 2.
t.se0adac4187: Let's settle four bunnies 🐰. One on the left, three on the right — four. Or two on the left, two on the right — four again! 4 is 1 and 3, or 2 and 2.
t.s2e1637a56f: Show five fingers ✋. Bend two — three stay open. Two and three — five! And also: one and four make five too. 5 is 2 and 3, or 1 and 4.
t.s36a083bb9a: I show one hand: five fingers. Now I hide some of them behind my back. You can see two on the screen — how many are hidden? Three! Because five is two and three. Now play this game with your mum and dad!
t.s8aaa154315: On the left 🔴, on the right 🔴🔴. How many altogether?
t.s92b97228df: That's right! One and two — three.
t.s9f1f5a0527: Great job! Two and two — four.
t.s31bdb14f8f: A hand has 5 fingers. 1 is bent. How many are open? ✋
t.s631d20cd5a: Super! Five is one and four.
t.s4be907b6da: Beep-beep! Six and seven built little houses too. They have more guests — butterflies and ladybugs. Who goes into which room? Let's settle them in!
t.sed820ac8f8: Six butterflies 🦋 landed on two flowers. Two on the first, four on the second — six in all. Or three and three — six again! 6 is 2 and 4, 3 and 3, or 1 and 5.
t.s2bd04a4e43: Seven ladybugs 🐞 climbed onto two leaves: three on one, four on the other. Three and four — seven! Or five fingers on one hand and two on the other ✋✌️ — seven again.
t.s6fa61995e6: «Six butterflies came flying, on two flowers they were lying. Three on this one, three on that — six in all, how about that?» Now flap your arms like wings, split into two groups and fly!
t.sadee896f3e: That's right! Three and three — six.
t.sf4c42a6c3f: Well done! Five and two — seven.
t.s61c3df52e0: On one leaf 🐞🐞🐞🐞, on the other 🐞🐞🐞. How many altogether?
t.s4dd77e744b: Great job! Four and three — seven.
t.sa24ca76f62: Beep-beep! Today there are two big houses: eight and nine. Little fish and stars came to visit them. Let's place them in fish tanks and in the sky!
t.s2df68280c4: Eight fish 🐟 were split into two tanks: four and four. Eight in all! Or five and three — eight again. 8 is 4 and 4, or 5 and 3.
t.s31d93535ec: There are nine stars in the sky ⭐. Five on the left, four on the right — nine! Five fingers on one hand, four on the other ✋🖖 — nine too. 9 is 5 and 4.
t.s8694aac4cb: That's right! Four and four — eight.
t.s0d5a749f6a: Well done! Five and four — nine.
t.s010af86475: In one tank 🐟🐟🐟🐟🐟🐟, in the other 🐟🐟. How many altogether?
t.s6db624fb02: Great job! Six and two — eight.
t.saea2b443ca: Beep-beep! Number ten is having a big birthday party and invited friends in pairs. Each pair together makes ten. Who are they? Let's find them with our fingers!
t.s9506cf6017: Ten's friend pairs: 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5. Open both hands 🙌 — ten fingers. Bend three — seven are open. Three and seven — ten!
t.s7b69beb22e: The easiest friends are five and five. Five on one hand, five on the other — ten! You can always see ten on your two hands 🙌.
t.s9b0ce2f531: I say a number — you say how many more make ten! Me: eight! You: two! Me: one! You: nine! Me: six! You: four! If it's tricky — look at your fingers. You're a true friend of ten!
t.sc94e64ae1c: That's right! Seven and three — ten.
t.sf289fe2ac3: Well done! Five and five — ten.
t.sd6dcdacf3d: Great job! Two and eight — ten.
t.s675cf336f9: Beep-beep! I opened the toy box. Inside there's a ball and a block. Why does the ball roll away, but the block stays put? Let's find out the secret together!
t.sd5152dab58: This is a sphere. It has no corners and no flat places anywhere — it is round all over. That's why a sphere rolls easily ⚽. A ball, a watermelon 🍉, the Earth 🌍 — they all look like a sphere.
t.s6057ace103: Turn a block around in your hand!
t.s617b39e400: This is a cube. It has six flat faces, and each face is a square. A cube has corners, so it doesn't roll — it stays put 🧊. A toy block, a sugar cube, an ice cube — they look like a cube.
t.s0c0c6de9a2: Put a ball and a toy block on the table. Gently push both with your finger. What happened? The ball rolled away, but the block slid a little and stopped. Because a sphere has no corners, but a cube does!
t.sdc357781e3: That's right! A sphere is round — it rolls.
t.sf93fc637a3: What shape does a watermelon look like? 🍉
t.sf3e11bba40: Well done! A watermelon looks like a sphere.
t.s0cf5274101: How many faces does a cube have?
t.sad58914ae2: Great job! A cube has six faces.
t.s4fa731b1b8: Which one looks like a cube?
t.s39bddf75eb: Super! A dice is a cube.
t.s44e9b72145: Beep-beep! Look around the kitchen: a glass, a jar... Look outside: a traffic cone, a party hat... These are shapes too! Today we'll meet two new shapes.
t.s0e0e372d80: This is a cylinder. It has flat circles on the top and bottom, and its side is round. Stand it up — it stays, lay it down — it rolls! A can 🥫, a glass, a pencil look like a cylinder.
t.se2b7d33815: Put your hands together over your head to make a point!
t.s3a69d6dbdc: This is a cone. It has a flat circle at the bottom, and at the top it ends in a sharp point. An ice cream cone 🍦, a traffic cone, a party hat 🥳 — they are all cones!
t.s54cbc7de14: You're the shopkeeper, I'm the customer! I say: «Give me something with a pointy top!» — you find the cone. «Give me something that rolls when it lies down and stands when you stand it up!» — a cylinder! «Something round all over!» — a sphere! Thank you, shopkeeper!
t.s02be402ce8: Which shape has a pointy top?
t.s61937ad728: That's right! A cone has a pointy top.
t.sdae111dde3: What shape does a can look like? 🥫
t.s1a3cabd33e: Well done! A can is a cylinder.
t.sae42ebfbc7: What shape is a party hat? 🥳
t.s88b83f7f7b: Great job! A party hat is a cone.
t.scf709117a7: Which shape has two flat circle sides?
t.s4dfc090a26: Super! A cylinder has a circle on top and on the bottom.
t.s5cbaedbc85: Beep-beep! The shapes want to have a race! But who can roll in the race, and who will stay put? Let's put them on a sloping board and see. What do you think?
t.s38fbdab9f6: Shapes with round sides roll. A sphere rolls in every direction ⚽. If we lay a cylinder down — it rolls straight too 🥫. And a cone rolls round and round in a circle.
t.s0f70a11341: Shapes with flat faces stay put. However you place a cube — it stands 🧊. If we stand a cylinder up — it stands too. That's why houses are built from bricks shaped like boxes 🧱!
t.sb88a7fceff: Lift one side of a book to make a slope. Put a ball, a block, a pencil and an ice cream cone (or a paper cone) on it. Which ones rolled down? Which one stayed? Tell your mum and dad what happened!
t.s67e66e501e: That's right! All of a cube's faces are flat.
t.sd3bb60a994: Which shape can both stand and roll?
t.s7e53810eb1: Well done! A cylinder stands when upright and rolls when lying down.
t.s9cfcc3c214: Which shape rolls in every direction?
t.sd938d7ba82: Great job! A sphere rolls in every direction.
t.s16334c4d5f: What shape does a brick look like? 🧱
t.s1cacec0a14: Super! A brick is flat like a box — it stands.
t.s42794e6db7: Beep-beep! Today we're detectives! We'll find the shapes hiding at home, outside and at kindergarten. Grab your magnifying glass — the search begins!
t.s7b283f7c90: Find one shape in the room and show it!
t.s33d2d09f83: There are lots of shapes at home! A ball — a sphere ⚽. A gift box — a cube 🎁. A glass — a cylinder 🥛. A party hat — a cone 🥳. Look around your room: what else is there?
t.sfdb44bf2ac: Let's build a castle from shapes 🏰! We'll put cubes at the bottom — they stand firmly. Cylinders for the towers, and cones on top of the towers — those are the roofs. And the sphere will be a ball to play with in front of the castle!
t.s6ce7819935: What shape is a gift box? 🎁
t.s6f710ddfa1: That's right! The box is a cube.
t.sa23b72a848: Which shape fits on top of a castle tower? 🏰
t.s4872e652fc: Well done! A cone is a pointy roof.
t.s67e8959142: Which thing looks like a cylinder?
t.s4c5252e114: Great job! A glass is a cylinder.
t.s58dcfcbcab: What shape does an orange look like? 🍊
t.se9d09dfb88: Super! An orange looks like a sphere.
t.scedca360cd: Beep-beep! Did you know days live together as a family? Their family is called a week. How many brothers are in the family? Today we'll meet the first three.
t.s5da8f5b49c: A week is seven days. After seven days go by, the week starts again. Remember, a rainbow has seven colours too 🌈? And a week has seven days!
t.sa3a5cdf25f: Monday is the first day of the week. After the weekend kids go to kindergarten and parents go to work. Remember: «Monday» means the first day!
t.s90721ef31b: Tuesday is the second day, Wednesday is the third. Remember the order: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday. It's like counting: one, two, three!
t.se01db56e40: The week is a train, and the days are the carriages! «Choo-choo! The first carriage is Monday, the second is Tuesday, the third is Wednesday!» Hold each other's shoulders, move like a train and count the carriages!
t.s083deb3669: How many days are in a week? 📅
t.sf7d6de4544: That's right! A week has seven days.
t.s28d93df917: What is the first day of the week?
t.s28c84ebd7a: Well done! Monday is the first day.
t.s68a7d425a6: Beep-beep! We need to hook four more carriages onto the train of days. Who are they? Two of them are everyone's favourite days, because we get to rest! Which ones?
t.s3135531695: Thursday is the fourth day, Friday is the fifth. On Friday the work week ends. The order: Wednesday, Thursday, Friday.
t.sd714f43c3b: Saturday is the sixth day, Sunday is the seventh, the last one. Lots of people rest on these days 🧺: we go for walks and visit friends. After Sunday comes Monday again!
t.sfda6ad0a51: Bend one finger for each day!
t.s3615710c74: Now let's say the whole week: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday! Bend one finger for each day — that makes seven!
t.s19f83d9aba: Which day of the week is Friday?
t.s96cd5bce10: That's right! Friday is the fifth day.
t.sfcb9fd502e: What is the last day of the week?
t.sb8af8e227f: Well done! Sunday is the seventh, last day.
t.scfeb16bc7d: Great job! The week starts again — Monday.
t.s09438593ea: Beep-beep! I'm a little bird, and I watch nature all year round. Sometimes it snows, sometimes flowers bloom, sometimes it's hot, sometimes leaves fall. These changes are the seasons! How many are there?
t.sf5e49c25cf: Winter is the coldest season. It snows ❄️, we build a snowman and go sledging. We wear warm clothes, a hat and mittens 🧤.
t.sbbcf819806: Spring is the season when nature wakes up. The snow melts, trees blossom 🌸, birds come back. The Navruz holiday comes in spring!
t.sf9365dbd5d: Summer is the hottest season. The sun shines brightly ☀️, we go swimming. Watermelons, cherries and grapes get ripe 🍉.
t.s35fde4e125: Autumn is harvest time. Leaves turn yellow and fall 🍂, it rains. People pick apples, pomegranates and cotton. In autumn children go to school!
t.s2b663e5fe6: I name a season — you act it out! Winter — shiver and rub your hands. Spring — be a flower, open your arms and grow. Summer — wave your arms like you're swimming. Autumn — be a leaf, spin and float down to the ground! Winter! Summer! Autumn! Spring!
t.sdce65718db: In which season does it snow? ❄️
t.s2fd4dae51c: That's right! It snows in winter.
t.sff0801a86a: In which season do leaves turn yellow and fall?
t.s80ea94c46d: Well done! Leaves fall in autumn.
t.s52ded3ea5b: In which season do watermelons get ripe? 🍉
t.s969008b5e1: How many seasons are in a year?
t.s42929a0cec: Super! Winter, spring, summer, autumn — four.
t.s12270d740d: Beep-beep! Seasons and days go round in a circle — one leaves, another comes. Today we'll spin the wheel of time. Which season comes after which?
t.s2f08a73942: The seasons always come in the same order: after winter comes spring, after spring summer, after summer autumn, and after autumn winter again ❄️🌷☀️🍂. Just like a spinning wheel!
t.s123939b96e: Today is the day we are living right now. What did you do today? Did you come to kindergarten? Did you play? All of that is today!
t.s30b64e0f92: Yesterday is the day before today, it has already passed ⬅️. Tomorrow is the day that comes after today ➡️. If today is Tuesday, yesterday was Monday, and tomorrow will be Wednesday!
t.sdc46175fd8: robot Kabu asks: «What did you do yesterday?» You answer: «Yesterday I played ...». «And today?» — «Today I ... ». «What will you do tomorrow?» — «Tomorrow I will ...». Talk like this with your mom and dad too!
t.s7af3eb72d9: Well done! After summer comes autumn.
t.s1496456797: Today is Wednesday. What day is tomorrow?
t.s6fc9ac44e4: Great job! After Wednesday comes Thursday.
t.s2ba8ccb797: Today is Friday. What day was yesterday?
t.sa92bf15a7c: Beep-beep! Two snakes became friends. One says: «I'm long!» The other says: «What about me?» How do we know who is longer? Let's lay them side by side!
t.s0e5ab3f59e: We put two things side by side, with their starts in one place. The one that reaches farther is long. A long snake 🐍, a long train 🚂, a long scarf 🧣.
t.s2e643edca0: When we put things side by side, the short one ends first. A pencil that got small from use is short ✏️. A short rope, a short tail 🐇.
t.sc58d19c353: To compare the right way, we put the starts of two things on one line. Otherwise our eyes can trick us! The starts are even — now we look at the ends.
t.s2a861ee99d: Which one is short: a new pencil or a small used one? ✏️
t.s3603efd3c8: Well done! The small used pencil is short.
t.sa930d6ad18: What do we do to compare two ribbons the right way?
t.s3a1b6b85ca: Great job! We put their starts on one line.
t.s7220819f74: Which animal has the longest neck?
t.sc0e8ed0dfd: Super! The giraffe has a long neck.
t.s6de6e85c6a: Beep-beep! How far is it from the door to the window in the room? We don't have a ruler. But we have feet! Let's measure with steps — it's so much fun!
t.s2406b2e3d9: To measure means to count how many same-size pieces fit. We step and count: one step, two steps, three steps 👣. However many steps from the door to the table — that's the distance!
t.s66c09824c3: If one path took eight steps and another took three steps, the eight-step path is farther. Many steps — far, few steps — near!
t.sdcca2fe89a: My dad's step is big, and mine is small. So Dad walked the same path in 4 steps, and I did it in 7 🐘🐭. To measure correctly, one person should measure with the same steps.
t.s6722b2fc25: Measure at home with your mom and dad: how many steps from the kitchen to the bedroom? And from the door to the sofa? Then let Dad measure too. Who got more? Why? Because your step is small!
t.s3bee1409d3: It's 5 steps to the door and 8 steps to the window. Which is farther?
t.sfbcfa91070: An elephant 🐘 and a mouse 🐭 walked the same path. Who takes more steps?
t.sb65f6eb4ad: Great job! The mouse's step is small, so it needs many steps.
t.s2bd2e3cd49: What is a path like if it took few steps?
t.s77ddb9d1fd: Beep-beep! How long is the table? We can't measure it with steps — we don't walk on tables! So our hand and a piece of string will help us.
t.sda0a350455: Spread your hand wide to make a hand span!
t.sf90bf7f22e: Open your hand wide 🖐️: from your thumb to your little finger is one hand span. We put the span on the table and measure one after another: one, two, three spans. How many spans long is the table?
t.sb32b8842b4: How do we measure something curvy? We lay a string along it, then straighten the string and compare it with something else 🧵. Long string — long thing!
t.s816ab67bdb: We draw a line on paper with a pencil. If we move the pencil a long way — a long line; just a little — a short line ✏️. We compare lines by lining up their starts too.
t.s8cfa9a55e9: What do we call the distance from the thumb to the little finger? 🖐️
t.s07afc96072: The table is 6 spans, the chair is 3 spans. Which one is longer?
t.sed1fd665ce: Well done! Six spans is longer.
t.s8b681829d7: What is handy for measuring a curvy path?
t.se523dae816: Great job! We lay a string along the path.
t.s553c6fe224: The book 🖐️🖐️ is two spans, the notebook 🖐️ is one span. Which one is shorter?
t.sd471c4328b: Beep-beep! I'm a little feather — I'm so light that the wind blows me away! And an elephant is so heavy that nobody can lift it. Heavy and light — what do they mean?
t.s9f56f413be: Heavy things are hard to lift, they pull your hands down. A watermelon 🍉, a brick 🧱, an elephant 🐘 are heavy. A big bucket of water is heavy too!
t.sc454a917bc: Light things are easy to lift. A feather 🪶, a balloon 🎈, paper are light. Even the wind can blow them away!
t.s08d73b8ed7: A balance scale has two pans ⚖️. The pan with the heavy thing goes down, and the pan with the light thing goes up. If both are equally heavy, the scale stays level.
t.s14b75ecc92: Hold both hands out in front of you like the pans of a scale. Put an apple in one hand and a nut in the other. Which hand is pulled down? That thing is heavier! Now compare a book and a pencil. Tell your mom and dad what you found!
t.s3547a55849: Well done! The feather is very light.
t.s61c002944e: One pan of the scale went down. What is the thing on it like?
t.s8e5c5af94e: Great job! The heavy pan goes down.
t.sbbcdc0fc90: The scale is level ⚖️. What are the things like?
t.s5836ba25ad: Super! A level scale means they're equal.
t.sf39f04b3d1: Beep-beep! A little mouse smelled some cheese, but between them is a tangle of paths — a maze! Shall we help it find the way?
t.s6781e74968: A maze is paths with lots of turns. Some paths run into a wall — that's a dead end. We follow the path with our finger; if we hit a dead end, we go back and try another one 🐭🧀.
t.s84f7847cc1: Raise your right hand — that's the right side 👉. Most people hold a spoon with their right hand. When we say «turn right» in the maze, we go toward our right hand.
t.s4186d507cf: Raise your left hand — that's the left side 👈. Our heart beats on the left ❤️. When we say «turn left», we go toward our left hand.
t.scbfa1d049c: You are the robot, and I'm the controller! «Two steps forward! Turn right! One step forward! Turn left! Stop!» A robot only moves on command. Now you give the commands, and let your mom and dad be the robots!
t.s374b05b559: In the maze, the path ran into a wall. What do we do?
t.sc2fd8d934f: Right! We go back and try another path.
t.s9ed84a5a9d: What will the mouse find when it gets out of the maze? 🐭
t.s670b051ea2: Beep-beep! I found a treasure map! There are no words on it, only arrows. If we go where the arrows point, we'll find the treasure! Come on, let's go!
t.s61d302d871: Up means toward the top, toward the sky ⬆️. Down means toward the ground ⬇️. Birds fly up high, flowers grow down low. Raise your hand up, now put it down!
t.se54dfd91b1: Wherever the arrow points, that's where we go. ➡️ — right, ⬅️ — left, ⬆️ — up, ⬇️ — down. Each arrow is one step!
t.s7d9e6a52ef: The map has a row of arrows: ➡️➡️⬆️. That means: two steps right, one step up. We point to each arrow with a finger and count — we won't get lost! 🏴‍☠️
t.sef4260b859: Ask your mom or dad to hide a toy in the room and draw arrows on paper: ⬆️⬆️⬆️ ➡️➡️. You step by the arrows: three steps forward, two steps right. Did you find the treasure? Well done, captain!
t.s35b8a60d2c: Path: ➡️➡️➡️. How many steps to the right?
t.sfea6803131: Great job! Three arrows — three steps.
t.sf80cfea7bd: Beep-beep! Someone sneaky dropped something into the fruit basket. It doesn't look like fruit at all! Let's find the odd guest and say why it doesn't belong.
t.s17b7decbe9: A group is things that are alike. An apple, a pear, a banana — a group of fruits 🍎🍐🍌. A ball, a cube, a cone — a group of shapes. We find what makes them alike: color, shape or kind.
t.s5ac602defb: The odd one out is the thing that doesn't fit the group. 🍎🍐🍌🚗 — the car is the odd one out, because it isn't a fruit! When we find the odd one, we always answer the question «why?».
t.s050ee3406d: I'll say three words — which one is the odd one out, and why? «Winter, summer, Monday» — Monday, because it's not a season, it's a day! «Three, five, apple» — apple, because it's not a number! Now you make up a puzzle for me!
t.s74ccc2aa58: Which one is the odd one out? 🍎 🍐 🍌 🚗
t.s8df774a0e8: Right! A car is not a fruit.
t.sf81d2bf2a4: Which one is the odd one out? 🐈 🐕 🐄 ✏️
t.s589a1bb582: Well done! A pencil is not an animal.
t.sef66d98543: Which one is the odd one out? ⚽ 🍊 🏀 🧊
t.s95e265e845: Great job! The cube isn't round, and the others look like a ball.
t.s1ebd752a80: Which one is the odd one out? ❄️ ⛄ 🧤 🍉
t.s04abbeb079: Super! The watermelon belongs to summer, the rest belong to winter.
t.sb51b9cbedf: Beep-beep! I'm stringing beads: red, yellow, red, yellow... Oops, I forgot the next one! Help me — this row has a secret rule!
t.s3b659f6164: In a pattern, things repeat by a rule. 🔴🟡🔴🟡 — red, yellow, red, yellow. The rule: red, then yellow! So the next one is red 🔴.
t.s73bd5d7fad: Let's say the pattern out loud: «cat, dog, cat, dog...» — our ears hear the rule too! 🐈🐕🐈🐕❓ Next comes the cat. Even if the row is long, the rule stays the same.
t.s9daf4306cf: Numbers can make a pattern too: 1, 2, 3, 4 — each is one more, the next is 5. Backward: 5, 4, 3 — the next is 2. Remember number neighbors? They will help!
t.s8b1cdeb3da: Let's make a pattern with moves! Clap, jump, clap, jump... What's next? Clap! Now a harder one: clap, clap, sit down; clap, clap, sit down... What's next? Clap! You're a logic master! Beep-beep!
t.s57b6139d91: Well done! After the dog comes the cat.
t.s9db2f09275: Great job! Each is one more — six.
t.sc2a02a0887: Super! The rule: ball, cube, cube — next is a cube.
t.s47a396190a: Hello, my friend! I'm robot Kabu. Beep-beep! You count to ten really well. But what comes after ten? Today we'll go up to the second floor of Number Land — big numbers live there!
t.sa75e5369ce: We count ten sticks and tie them with a ribbon — that's one ten 🎀. Now we don't have to count to ten every time — we see the bundle and know: it's ten! Big numbers are made of tens and ones.
t.sb989d4bf82: Let's add one more stick to the ten — that makes eleven. It is written with two digits: 1 and 1. The first 1 is the ten, the second 1 is one one. Ten and one — eleven!
t.s108d0699be: A ten and two sticks — twelve. We write: 1 and 2. On a clock face, the biggest number is twelve 🕛. And there are twelve months in a year too!
t.s8736550b1d: Find ten pencils or sticks at home and tie them with a rubber band — that's a ten! Now put one pencil next to it: eleven. One more: twelve. Show your mom and dad and say: «One ten and two ones — twelve!»
t.s11328d9a30: What do we call ten sticks tied together? 🎀
t.sb17f53849e: A ten and 1 more stick. How many in all?
t.s840f040a23: Well done! Ten and one — eleven.
t.se9009f1fad: How many tens are in the number 12?
t.sc052426ff2: Great job! 12 is one ten and two ones.
t.s22a2bc1b1e: Beep-beep! There are three more rooms on the second floor. One ten lives in each room, but the guest ones are different. Let's knock on the door: knock-knock!
t.s9083792be6: A ten and three ones — thirteen. We write: first 1 (the ten), then 3 (the ones). Ten fingers on two hands and three toes on a foot — thirteen!
t.s8e85fd1b41: A ten and four ones — fourteen. We write: 1 and 4. Remember, four looks like an upside-down chair? Now it stands next to the ten!
t.s33eeb90711: A ten and five ones — fifteen. Two hands (ten) and one more hand (five) — three hands have fifteen fingers! If three kids raise their hands, you see fifteen fingers 🙌✋.
t.s5cc0fbc465: A ten and 🥢🥢🥢🥢. How many in all?
t.se3437e453b: How many ones are in the number 15 (besides the ten)?
t.s20e141d21b: Well done! 15 is a ten and five ones.
t.s3b32aa13bf: Beep-beep! We're climbing up the number staircase. Each step is one more. Don't look down, let's go up — 16, 17, 18!
t.s0eb12291e6: A ten and six ones — sixteen. We write: 1 and 6. The little snail six came to stand by the ten!
t.sb515c38540: A ten and seven ones — seventeen. We write: 1 and 7. A week has seven days — a ten and one week make seventeen!
t.s4807bc7ea9: Lift your foot for each number, like stepping up a stair!
t.sd686619b62: A ten and eight ones — eighteen. We write: 1 and 8. Count: sixteen, seventeen, eighteen — each step is one more!
t.sdbd5b2e7c7: «Eleven, twelve — up the stairs we go, thirteen, fourteen — higher, don't be slow, fifteen, sixteen — stop and catch your breath, seventeen, eighteen — almost at the top!» With each number, step in place like climbing a stair!
t.sb8895cd2bb: A ten and 🥢🥢🥢🥢🥢🥢🥢. How many in all?
t.s4857da1bbc: Beep-beep! We've reached the very top of the stairs! Two bundles of ten are waiting for us up there. Two tens together — what number is that? Let's find out!
t.s4a2b7345ad: A ten and nine ones — nineteen. We write: 1 and 9. If we add one more one, the second ten will be full!
t.s19f15ae864: We tie ten ones together again — now we have two tens 🎀🎀. That's twenty! We write: 2 and 0. The 2 means two tens, the 0 means no extra ones. We have twenty fingers and toes in all!
t.s28854bc32e: Clap your hands and count to twenty!
t.sd265c5a1e6: Now we can count to twenty: one, two ... ten, eleven ... nineteen, twenty! We can count backward too: twenty, nineteen, eighteen... Each step is one less.
t.s56ab89a054: Now our rocket is really big! Let's count backward from twenty. Squat down and start: twenty, nineteen, eighteen ... ten, nine ... three, two, one, ZERO! Jump — blast off! 🚀
t.s9aa22bf9d3: 🎀🔟 🎀🔟 — two tens. What number is it?
t.s2ca769cd0b: Super! Nineteen comes later when we count — it's bigger.
t.s154d988c9f: Beep-beep! I brought two apples in one basket and one apple in another. If we put them all into one big basket, how many will there be? To write this down, math has special signs!
t.scd2f220ca2: Adding means putting two groups together. We put 🍎🍎 and 🍎 into one basket — now there are 🍎🍎🍎, three! When we add, we get more.
t.s716d55a9d7: Cross two fingers to make a plus!
t.sc430742cba: We write adding with the «plus» sign: ➕. It looks like two crossed sticks — like a hand waving «add!» We write 2 + 1 and read it «two plus one».
t.se3c7b599d7: The «equals» sign is two flat lines 🟰. It means «here is the answer». 2 + 1 = 3: two plus one equals three. Both sides of the equals sign have the same amount!
t.s3c6f010f05: Take two pencils. Hold one standing up, lay the other one down, and cross them — plus ➕! Now lay both down, one above the other — equals 🟰! Put 2 spoons on the table, plus, 1 spoon, equals. Show the answer with spoons!
t.s3e98b54780: 🍎🍎 and 🍎 together — how many is that?
t.sb9ca9fd65d: Well done! Plus means we add.
t.s44e71665a2: Which sign means «here is the answer»?
t.s912b3aa3fd: What happens to things when we add?
t.s4c699cd4fd: Super! When we add, we get more.
t.s2e3dac8b24: Beep-beep! Little ducks are swimming to the lake. One, then one more... Shall we say how many there are each time? Let's remember how numbers are made up — and now we'll write it with a plus!
t.s20c4c91840: Adding one is super easy: just say the next number! 🐤🐤🐤 + 🐤 — after three comes four. So 3 + 1 = 4. 4 + 1 = 5. Neighbor numbers help us!
t.sab2c00997e: Look at the picture: 🎈🎈 and 🎈🎈🎈. The first group is 2, the second is 3. The sum: 2 + 3. Let's count them all: five. 2 + 3 = 5. Remember, 5 is 2 and 3!
t.sd4c4810997: «One little duck swims on the lake, one more comes — now there are two! Two little ducks swim on the lake, one more comes — now there are three!» Let's sing like this up to five. Each time a new duck comes, open one finger!
t.se0a487a99d: Well done! After four comes five.
t.sf7d3094570: Beep-beep! Bigger sums are here! How do we solve 6 + 3? Counting everything from the start takes long. I'll teach you a magic trick — counting on from the bigger number!
t.s981d4296e4: Keep six «in your head» and count on with three fingers!
t.s56e94e5007: In 6 + 3 we keep the bigger number, 6, in our head 🧠. Then we open three fingers and count on: seven, eight, nine! 6 + 3 = 9. No need to count the six again!
t.s48a87b904a: 5 + 2: five fingers on one hand ✋, two on the other ✌️. Count on from five: six, seven. 5 + 2 = 7. Your fingers are always with you!
t.s3bf2379541: A ten-box has 7 buttons in it. How many empty squares are left? Three! So 7 + 3 = 10. Remember the friends of ten: 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5.
t.sc5f949e12b: That's right! Six... seven, eight, nine.
t.s3307bd3368: Great job! 8 and 2 are friends of ten.
t.scf399d0744: Beep-beep! We have two secrets! The first: what happens if we add nothing? The second: if we swap the numbers, does the answer change? Let's find out!
t.sa0d9c1c272: There are 🍪🍪🍪🍪🍪 five cookies on a plate. Mom passed an empty plate — nothing was added. Still five! 5 + 0 = 5. When we add zero, the number stays the same.
t.s8056568a5d: 🍎🍎 + 🍎🍎🍎🍎🍎 = 7. Now let's swap the baskets: 🍎🍎🍎🍎🍎 + 🍎🍎 = 7. The answer is seven again! When the numbers swap places, the sum stays the same. It's easier to count with the bigger number first!
t.s7f315b3f87: That's right! Add zero — nothing changes.
t.s3f125c3608: Well done! Swap them, and the answer stays the same.
t.sb95f114afc: Great job! Nothing was added — four.
t.sf72d28f38b: How can we write 1 + 8 to make it easy?
t.s313b919d8c: Super! 8 + 1 = 9 — we start with the bigger number.
t.s732504ec78: Beep-beep! Five sparrows were sitting on a branch. Suddenly a cat came — two of them flew away, flutter-flutter! How many are left? Taking away answers this question.
t.sd65097688f: Taking away means taking part of what you have. From 🐦🐦🐦🐦🐦 two flew away — 🐦🐦🐦 are left. When we take away, we get fewer!
t.s364ede70f8: Hold one finger flat to show a minus!
t.sd501c34d2a: We write taking away with the «minus» sign: ➖. It's one flat line — like a plus with its standing stick taken away! 5 − 2 = 3: five minus two equals three.
t.s71531124b5: Five children are five sparrows sitting on a branch (on chairs). I'll be the cat and say «Meow!» — two sparrows fly away. Let's count who's left: three! Robot Kabu writes: 5 − 2 = 3. Now let's play with another number!
t.saf6fa0988f: 🐦🐦🐦🐦🐦 were sitting, 2 flew away. How many are left?
t.s4ea671488b: Well done! Minus means we take away.
t.s16762188c3: What happens to things when we take away?
t.s4311d1644b: Great job! When we take away, we get fewer.
t.s0ca7a8cb0d: 🍬🍬🍬🍬 were here, we ate 1. How many are left?
t.s965446faa2: Beep-beep! There are apples on a plate, and we eat one every day. To say quickly how many are left, we know a secret — the number before!
t.sf90a2405b8: Taking away one is easy: just say the number before! 🍏🍏🍏🍏 − 🍏: the number before four is three. 4 − 1 = 3. Remember counting backward!
t.s1aa3f11843: There were 🍩🍩🍩 three donuts on a plate. We ate all three — the plate is totally empty! 3 − 3 = 0. Take them all, and zero is left. What if we take nothing? 3 − 0 = 3!
t.sea1ea02235: That's right! The number before five is four.
t.s2561299b35: Well done! We ate them all — zero.
t.sbaa630979e: Great job! Two went away from four — two are left.
t.s426fb1e90c: Beep-beep! Now big problems: 9 − 3, 10 − 4. How can we solve them fast? We have two magic tricks: counting backward and the friends of ten!
t.s991ebf0b1e: Fold a finger each time you jump back!
t.s5dabb78dbf: 9 − 3: we keep nine in our head and jump three steps back 🐸: eight, seven, six. 9 − 3 = 6. Fold one finger for each jump!
t.s1ab92d7074: 10 − 4: fold four of your ten fingers — six are left 🙌. Because 4 and 6 are friends of ten! 10 − 4 = 6. 10 − 7 = 3, because 7 and 3 are friends.
t.scf9c470024: Put the numbers from 0 to 10 in a row on the floor (on sheets of paper). You're a frog! I say «From 8, 3 jumps back!» — and you jump: seven, six, five. Where did you stop? On five! 8 − 3 = 5. Ribbit-ribbit!
t.s81b1aa73f2: Well done! 4 and 6 are friends of ten.
t.se451b8ee58: 🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈 were here, 2 popped. How many are left?
t.s74fc116d1d: Beep-beep! I wrote some sums, but the wind blew the signs away! 3 ❓ 2 = 5. Do we need a plus here, or a minus? Who can find it?
t.sdd87ee1159: If things came, were added or were given — there are more. So it's a plus ➕! «There were 3 children on the playground, 2 more came» — 3 + 2 = 5.
t.s1bf20c6d81: If things went away, were eaten or flew away — there are fewer. So it's a minus ➖! «There were 5 children, 2 went home» — 5 − 2 = 3.
t.s1928dc8449: 3 ❓ 2 = 5 — the answer got bigger, so there are more: plus! 3 + 2 = 5 ✅. If we put a minus: 3 − 2 = 1, and that's not five ❌. Both sides of the equals sign must be the same!
t.s267fb1eec4: There were 4 birds in the garden, and 3 more flew in. Which sum is it?
t.s45f685b984: Beep-beep! I'll tell you a little story and ask a question at the end. In math, a story with a question is called a «word problem». A word problem has three parts — let's get to know them!
t.sa119c2db70: The story is what the problem tells us: what there is and what happened. «There are 3 apples on the tree and 2 apples on the ground». Numbers hide in the story — let's listen carefully 👂.
t.s0a17ae11b9: The question is what we need to find. «How many apples are there in all?» There's no problem without a question! We listen to the question and think: do we add or take away?
t.s1a310a99ce: The answer is a full sentence that answers the question. We don't just say «five», we say «There are 5 apples in all». 3 + 2 = 5 is the solution, «5 apples» is the answer!
t.sbcae639644: «There are 4 pears in the basket.» Which part of the problem is it?
t.sfa82f59eb8: That's right! It's the story part.
t.sc395b40d25: «How many in all?» Which part is it?
t.s6d308d3185: There are 🍎🍎🍎 on the tree and 🍎🍎 on the ground. How many apples in all?
t.s9947cc135f: «There are 5 apples in all.» Which part is it?
t.s6635284e6d: Beep-beep! Guests are coming to our kindergarten. Someone brought a toy, someone brought a present. How many are there in all? This question calls for adding!
t.sf5de78fdbf: «Ali has 3 cars, Salim has 4. How many together?» The words «together» and «in all» are adding clues! 3 + 4 = 7. Answer: 7 cars together 🚗.
t.sd2a0437956: «2 cats were lying on the rug. 3 more cats came. How many are there now?» They came — more — plus! 2 + 3 = 5. Answer: 5 cats 🐈.
t.sa42df25f2d: Ali has 🚗🚗🚗, Salim has 🚗🚗🚗🚗. How many cars together?
t.sfed1c3d24d: 🐈🐈 are lying on the rug, and 🐈🐈🐈 more came. How many are there now?
t.s79f6bc7bec: Great job! «In all» and «together» mean adding.
t.s28686e9f80: Mom brought 6 apples, and Dad brought 4. How many in all?
t.s55066ed380: Beep-beep! A boy holding balloons is walking in the park. Oh no, the wind blew, and the balloons are flying away! How many will be left? Taking away answers this question.
t.s26b6167198: «The boy had 6 balloons. 2 flew away. How many are left?» «Left», «went away», «flew away» are taking-away words! 6 − 2 = 4. Answer: 4 balloons are left.
t.sff80a0446f: «The bunny had 8 carrots. It ate 3. How many are left?» It ate them — fewer — minus! 8 − 3 = 5. Answer: 5 carrots are left 🥕.
t.sd5b5b850ce: I'm the seller, and you're the shopper. There are 7 apples on the counter. You bought 2. How many are left on the counter? Five! Now you be the seller: how much fruit there was, how much you sold, how much is left — tell me yourself!
t.s8b2666e491: The boy has 🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈. 2 flew away. How many are left?
t.s3635024315: The bunny has 🥕🥕🥕🥕🥕🥕🥕🥕. It ate 3. How many are left?
t.s5c5bf4882c: Great job! «Left» and «went away» mean taking away.
t.s39790784f1: There were 10 birds on a branch. 4 flew away. How many are left?
t.s17ba727ec9: Beep-beep! Now you'll be the teacher! I'll show a picture, and you'll make up a story problem for it. Let your mom and dad solve it — and you check!
t.s5ee5be3069: Look at the picture: 4 ducks are on the lake 🦆, and 2 more are flying in. Let's make a problem: «There were 4 ducks on the lake. 2 more flew in. How many are there now?» There's a story, there's a question — the problem is ready!
t.s3f67dfd0be: You can make a problem from a sum too! 7 − 3: «There were 7 teddy bears in a box. I gave 3 to my friend. How many are left?» Every sum has a story hiding inside.
t.s43ebcc3a2a: Once we find the answer, we check it: count the picture again 🔍. When adding, the answer should be bigger; when taking away, it should be smaller. If it's right — well done!
t.s7cc01c3d7a: At dinner, make up a problem for your family! For example: «There were 4 flatbreads on the table. Dad brought 2 more flatbreads. How many are there now?» Whoever answers right — draw them a star ⭐. Who will collect the most stars?
t.s0eaafab1b1: There are 🦆🦆🦆🦆 on the lake, and 🦆🦆 more flew in. Which sum fits?
t.s8ce6e3b4f2: «There were 7 teddy bears in the box, I gave away 3.» Which sum?
t.se7331e1de8: 5 + 3 = ? Answer the problem: «There were 5 apples, 3 more came.»
t.se655c8338d: What happens to the answer when we add?
t.s873ce8bef1: Super! When we add, the number gets bigger.
t.s4abdb187c8: Beep-beep! I drew a house: walls at the bottom, a roof on top. What shape is the wall? And the roof? Let's count their corners and find their names!
t.sfdf4aabe41: A triangle has three corners and three sides 🔺. Count the corners with your finger: one, two, three! A roof, a slice of watermelon and a road sign look like triangles.
t.seb7e529586: A square has four corners and four sides, and all its sides are the same 🟥. Remember, the faces of a cube were squares! A chessboard square is a square too.
t.s53c3f06d82: A rectangle also has four corners, but two sides are long and two are short ▭. A door 🚪, a book, a phone — they're rectangles.
t.s4a7c7d935b: Take six sticks or pencils. Make a triangle from three of them 🔺. Make a square from four 🟥. Now make a rectangle from two long and two short pencils! How many sticks did you use? Count them!
t.s2ff5b3c86f: How many corners does a triangle have?
t.s863852bca4: That's right! A triangle has three corners.
t.s9136ec2f0f: Which shape has 4 corners and all sides the same?
t.s4d7d3e5856: What shape does a door look like? 🚪
t.s349443bb5b: Great job! A door is a rectangle.
t.s5c66a9a7aa: What shape is a house roof? 🏠
t.s9b77735ffd: Super! The roof is a triangle.
t.sc1cd37e444: Beep-beep! Look at a honeycomb: its cells have a funny shape — with six corners! Shapes with many corners are called «polygons». Let's count!
t.s795d0fc057: A corner is the pointy place where two lines meet. A side is the straight line between two corners. Every polygon has as many corners as sides!
t.s5c4e26798d: A pentagon has five corners and five sides ⬟. If we put a triangle roof on a square, we get a pentagon house! Count the corners: one, two, three, four, five.
t.sba522f8bcb: A hexagon has six corners and six sides ⬡. The cells in a honeycomb are hexagons 🐝🍯. A circle is just a circle, it has no corners — it's not a polygon!
t.s1ea777eee9: Look around the room: how many four-sided shapes can you find? A window, a door, a book, a TV... What about triangles? If you find a hexagon, you're a super hunter! Count the corners of what you found with your finger.
t.s48ab51b5ef: What shape is a honeycomb cell? 🐝
t.s864ea30694: How many sides does a pentagon have?
t.s0a92107f82: Great job! A circle has no corners.
t.s220badaa58: How many corners does a square have?
t.s31c95d3271: Beep-beep! Two friends found one apple. How should they share it so nobody is sad? Let's learn the secret of sharing fairly!
t.s4bcf698a6a: Sharing equally means the pieces are the same size. If one piece is big and the other is small — that's not equal, it's not fair! If we put the pieces on top of each other, they should cover each other exactly.
t.s7192313294: Fold the paper in the middle to make a half!
t.s337b62fd07: If we split a whole into two equal pieces, each piece is a half 🌓. Two halves together make a whole again! Half an apple, half a flatbread, half a square.
t.s1660aae93e: A whole is something not split yet: a whole apple 🍎, a whole flatbread 🍞. Split the whole, and you get pieces. Put the pieces together, and it's a whole again.
t.sd07c2d36da: Take a square sheet of paper. Fold it in the middle and cut — two rectangles! Put them on top of each other — they're equal. Fold another sheet from corner to corner — you get two triangles! They're equal halves too.
t.s40d5e95227: How can we share an apple fairly between two friends? 🍎
t.sc61ed101ce: What do two halves make together?
t.sa6d5519f99: Well done! Two halves make one whole.
t.s87656f7b18: A cookie was split into two equal parts. What do we call one part? 🍪
t.s1520fe3408: Great job! That is a half.
t.sd3948d780d: How can we check that the parts are equal?
t.s3cdf8b1fb8: Super! We put one on top of the other and compare.
t.sf227c70800: Beep-beep! Four friends came to the birthday party, but there is only one cake! If we cut it in half, there is only enough for two. How can we share it among four? A quarter will help us!
t.s91b2864d4f: If we split a whole into four equal parts, each part is a quarter 🍕. First we cut the cake in half, then cut each half in half again — four quarters! One for each friend.
t.s7586600abd: Put four quarters together and you get a whole cake again 🎂. Two quarters together make a half! A quarter is smaller than a half, because the whole was cut into more parts.
t.s09d375b501: Cut a circle out of paper — this is the cake! Fold it in half, then in half again, and cut. How many pieces did you get? Four quarters! Now give one to each toy: the teddy bear, the bunny, the doll and yourself. Everyone gets the same!
t.s0bdf2cd729: A pizza was cut into 4 equal parts. What is one part called? 🍕
t.s97f4620fd6: How many quarters together make a whole?
t.sf11b56048d: Well done! Four quarters make a whole.
t.sc558e2b225: Which part is bigger: a half or a quarter?
t.s5c5a53b361: Great job! A half is bigger than a quarter.
t.s730f20ef45: What do two quarters make together?
t.s31c31f9a14: Super! Two quarters make a half.
t.s614adb1855: Beep-beep! Tick-tock, tick-tock! What is that sound? It's the clock on the wall! It tells us when to get up, when to eat and when to sleep. Let's learn its language!
t.scaaf37b222: The clock face is the round face of the clock. The numbers from 1 to 12 are written around it in a circle 🕰️. At the very top is 12, at the bottom is 6. The hands go around and point to these numbers.
t.sd81f9e37ef: Show your short arm — the little hand!
t.s789ef9f2d0: The little hand is short and thick. It moves slowly and shows the hour. If the little hand points to 3, it is three o'clock! We call it the «hour hand».
t.sec5c88c904: The big hand is long and thin. It moves faster. When the big hand is on 12, it is exactly on the hour — «o'clock». Stretch out both arms: one short, one long — now you are a clock!
t.sabca24a3b3: What do we call the clock's face with numbers? 🕰️
t.s7cfbefc7b3: Well done! The little hand shows the hour.
t.sbd5c525864: Which number is at the very top of the clock face?
t.s4d48619771: Great job! At the top is 12.
t.s88133d0d76: Which hand is long and thin?
t.s7940f3a81e: Super! The big hand is long.
t.s965a527e26: Beep-beep! Robot Kabu's day: he wakes up at 7 o'clock, flies to kindergarten at 8 o'clock and has lunch at 1 o'clock. How do we see these times on a clock? The secret is simple!
t.s1aee26d092: To tell the time on the hour, first we look at the big hand: is it on 12? Yes! So it is exactly o'clock. Now we look at the little hand — whatever number it points to, that's the hour!
t.s900fe7b99b: The big hand is on 12, the little hand is on 3 — three o'clock 🕒. That's the afternoon: at kindergarten we get up after nap time and drink tea.
t.s43cf04eef1: Show the clock hands with your arms!
t.s9073e1ac6a: The big hand is on 12, the little hand is on 8 — eight o'clock 🕗. At eight in the morning we go to kindergarten or school. And at eight in the evening we get ready for bed.
t.s18847df5e6: Write the numbers from 1 to 12 on a paper plate. Cut a short hand and a long hand out of cardboard and pin them in the middle. Now I say a time and you show it: 7 o'clock! 2 o'clock! 12 o'clock! What time do you get up in the morning? Show that time!
t.scda47ba336: 🕒 The big hand is on 12, the little hand is on 3. What time is it?
t.s02a252ad67: Which hand tells us it is exactly on the hour?
t.sf4f2aa9603: Well done! When the big hand is on 12, it's exactly on the hour.
t.s3f662c410f: 🕗 The little hand is on 8. What time is it?
t.s00e93e6ea0: If it is 5 o'clock, which number does the little hand point to?
t.se4337d70a2: Super! The little hand is on 5.
t.s26c5f762dc: Beep-beep! Remember, there are four seasons: winter, spring, summer and autumn. Three months live in each season! Four seasons with three months each — how many months in all? Let's find out!
t.scd91050201: A year is twelve months. Each season has three months: four seasons make twelve months. The year starts in January and ends in December. Then a new year comes 🎄!
t.s7a8db7b712: The winter months are December, January and February ❄️. At the end of December comes the New Year holiday! January is the first month of the year. February is the last month of winter.
t.scf89d10777: The spring months are March, April and May 🌷. In March we celebrate Navruz and Mother's Day! In April the trees blossom, and in May everything around is green, green, green.
t.s4429651322: Let's stand in a circle, walk and sing: «December, January, February — snow is falling, let's build a snowman, merry! March and April, then comes May — flowers bloom and birds fly home to stay!» Take a step on each month's name!
t.s57e2a71ef9: How many months are in a year? 🗓️
t.sddd5967ef1: Which is the first month of the year?
t.sed7199cd81: Which month is a winter month?
t.s566420d55d: Super! February is a winter month.
t.sd4a62d7b49: Beep-beep! Two more seasons are left — summer and autumn. Which months do they have? And most important: in which month will you go to school? Let's find out with the calendar!
t.s6123a9c672: The summer months are June, July and August ☀️. In June there's a holiday for children — June 1! July is the hottest month. In August watermelons and melons are so tasty 🍉.
t.sa552b997e9: The autumn months are September, October and November 🍂. September 1 is Knowledge Day, when children go to school 🎒! In October the leaves turn yellow, and in November the cold begins.
t.s5517762105: A calendar is a chart with all the days of the year 📅. It shows the name of the month, the days of the week and the dates. Circle your birthday on the calendar and count the days until it comes!
t.sed94344294: In which month do children go to school? 🎒
t.s2e8a9a131a: Which month is a summer month?
t.s7ab646af11: Well done! July is a summer month.
t.sa81d592f0e: What do we call a chart with days and months? 📅
t.sbb969d00a5: Great job! That is a calendar.
t.s2983124851: Beep-beep! At school you will get a squared notebook. The tiny squares in it are called cells. They are little houses for maths! Today we'll go on a trip across the cells.
t.sbfdcd56458: A cell is a tiny square in the notebook 🔲. One digit lives in each cell. We count the cells and put the pencil in the right spot. At school we write numbers neatly in the cells!
t.s67c198aab6: The pencil walks along the lines of the cells. «2 cells right» — we move the pencil two cells to the right ➡️. «1 cell up» — one cell up ⬆️. Remember the arrow path?
t.s339611556e: Raise the hand you hold your pencil with!
t.sa156c68dd9: On the left side of the notebook there's a margin — an empty space, and we write towards the right. We hold the pencil in the right hand (some people use the left). Right is ➡️, left is ⬅️, remember?
t.s3ca8d7219d: What do we call a tiny square in the notebook? 🔲
t.sd24781ea03: «3 cells right» — where does the pencil go?
t.s75eb6daa2d: Well done! Three cells to the right.
t.s9f99273064: «1 cell down» — which arrow is it?
t.s6bcf3cae52: What shape does a cell look like?
t.s6372de8df0: Super! A cell is a small square.
t.sf6101f4805: Beep-beep! I made up a magic dictation: I only say arrows and numbers, and you draw — at the end a picture appears! What will it be? Get your pencil ready!
t.s0c5a8fa17c: In a grid dictation I say: «1 ➡️, 1 ⬆️, 1 ➡️, 1 ⬆️». With each command you move your pencil. Look — a staircase appears 🪜! You need to listen carefully and count.
t.s11867a189a: A pattern is a picture that repeats. «2 ⬆️, 2 ➡️, 2 ⬇️, 2 ➡️» — and again from the start! You get a castle wall with teeth 🏰. Once we find the rule, we can keep the pattern going to the end of the notebook. Remember logic rows?
t.s8e49724e51: Put a dot in your squared notebook. Listen, I'm saying: 3 cells right ➡️. 3 cells down ⬇️. 3 cells left ⬅️. 3 cells up ⬆️. What did you get? A square! Draw a smiling face inside it 🙂.
t.s97e8ce80a8: Well done! The rule is: up, right, down, right.
t.s5655087a09: To draw a square: 2 ➡️, 2 ⬇️, 2 ⬅️ ... and then?
t.sf2added753: Great job! We go back up and close the square.
t.sfa39276da1: Beep-beep! I want to go to the shop, and coins are jingling in my pocket. But how much is each coin worth? The money of Uzbekistan is the soum! Let's get to know it.
t.sfad8c86b0d: A coin is round metal money 🪙. Each coin has a number on it — it tells how much the coin is worth. Our money is the soum. Don't put coins in your mouth, and wash your hands after playing!
t.sbd0db2a59e: This is a one-hundred-soum coin. It has a 1 and two zeros on it: 100. Two hundred-coins make two hundred soums, three hundred-coins make three hundred soums! Let's count: one hundred, two hundred, three hundred.
t.sf63963ee35: A two-hundred-soum coin is worth two hundred-coins. A five-hundred-soum coin is worth five hundred-coins! Coins can be swapped: one two-hundred coin = two hundred-coins.
t.sdf3cc05f3b: What do we call round metal money?
t.s8e1373c63d: Well done! The money of Uzbekistan is the soum.
t.s276419b3e3: Three one-hundred-soum coins 🪙🪙🪙. How much in all?
t.s5305cb1d34: Great job! One hundred, two hundred, three hundred.
t.scb1d2ea781: How many hundred-coins is one two-hundred coin worth?
t.sa496ab7d6f: Beep-beep! Today we're opening a shop! I'm the seller and you're the shopper. All prices are in hundred-coins. If you count right, the purchase is yours!
t.s3c537a162d: A price is how much something costs 🏷️. In our shop: an apple is 2 hundred-coins, a balloon is 3 hundred-coins, a book is 5 hundred-coins. We count the price by the number of coins.
t.s698eaa8834: A balloon costs 3 hundred-coins. We count the coins out to the seller one by one: one, two, three 🪙🪙🪙. How much do the apple and the balloon cost together? 2 + 3 = 5 hundred-coins!
t.sc27d754ad3: There were 7 hundred-coins in the purse. We paid 5 for the book. How many are left? 7 − 5 = 2 hundred-coins 👛. Working out what's left is subtraction!
t.sca1f56dbb2: Put prices on your toys at home: from 1 to 5 hundred-coins. Buttons or paper circles can be the coins. Everyone takes 10 coins. Go shopping and count each time: how many did you pay, how many are left? Who has the most coins left at the end?
t.sb3cf9340d5: Apple 🍎 — 2 hundred-coins, balloon 🎈 — 3 hundred-coins. How many hundred-coins together?
t.s311f7930dc: There are 7 hundred-coins in the purse, and we paid 5. How many are left? 👛
t.s02723c12c8: What do we call how much something costs? 🏷️
t.s39d277ed39: Great job! That is the price.
t.s9de2d96729: You have 4 hundred-coins. The book costs 5 hundred-coins. Is it enough? 📕
t.s0f8513eb7a: Super! Four is less than five — not enough.
t.saef6b8f343: Beep-beep! Yesterday it rained — and today there are puddles outside! Why is that? Everything that happens has a reason. Today we'll be detectives and look for the answer to «why?».
t.s5a6ce1a3f9: A cause tells us why something happened. It rained 🌧️ — that's the cause. To find the cause, we ask: «Why?»
t.sf33845b55c: An effect is what happened after the cause. It rained — the effect: puddles appeared 💧. It snowed — the effect: we built a snowman. Ice cream was left in the sun — it melted! 🍦
t.sfc7e256167: Things happen in order: first we plant a seed 🌰, then we water it 💧, and at the end a flower grows 🌷. You can't mix up the order — a flower can't grow before the seed!
t.s211b79d5f3: Take two pieces of ice. Put one on a sunny windowsill and the other in the shade. Look at the clock and check after an hour. Which one melted faster? Why? The cause is the sun's warmth, the effect is the ice melting!
t.s0466ba87d6: Ice cream was left in the sun for a long time 🍦☀️. What will happen?
t.s49e595b62c: Right! It melts from the heat.
t.sd5d4d0fcdb: There are puddles outside 💧. What is the cause?
t.s1bf9bbee53: A glass fell off the table onto the floor 🥛. What is the effect?
t.s23bcac1191: Super! The glass might break or the water might spill.
t.s8ed422b2a8: Beep-beep! I have a magic staircase, but I don't jump one step at a time — I jump two steps at once! Can you guess which steps I'll land on? That's a pattern!
t.sf83f7cf014: A pattern is a rule that keeps repeating in a row. 🔺🟥🟥🔺🟥🟥 — the rule: one triangle, two squares. Once we find the rule, we can tell what goes in any spot!
t.sa551f6429e: Shoes come in pairs 👟👟. Let's count by twos: two, four, six, eight, ten! Each time it's two more. It's a faster way to count!
t.s5116adb63c: A row can also grow: 🟦, 🟦🟦, 🟦🟦🟦 ... one more each time. Next come four cubes! With numbers: 1, 3, 5, 7 — two more each time, so next is 9.
t.s94f57229a5: Lay paper numbers from 0 to 10 on the floor. Stand on zero. Now jump by twos, skipping one each time, and say: two, four, six, eight, ten! Now back again: ten, eight, six, four, two, zero! Well done, little kangaroo!
t.sa419c746aa: Counting by twos: 2, 4, 6, ... What comes next?
t.s39132fd094: Well done! After the triangle comes a square.
t.s2dee0fd38a: Great job! Two more each time — nine.
t.s454f8fd545: Super! Two less each time — four.
t.s98013cb1e8: Beep-beep! There was a running race at kindergarten! A bunny, a tortoise and a fox took part. Who came first, who came second, and who came last? Let's learn to say the order!
t.sb7f9b5f9df: First is the one standing at the very front of the line 🥇. In a race, whoever comes first is the winner. The child who is first in the line is closest to the door.
t.sd63701d2ce: After first comes second 🥈, then third 🥉. Order words come from ordinary numbers: two — second, three — third, five — fifth!
t.s3531e248d7: Last is the one standing at the very back of the line 🐢. The tortoise came last, but she didn't give up — she reached the finish line! There's nobody behind the last one in the line.
t.s87d6ac45e4: Line up with your family — let's be a train! You're at the front — the first carriage. «Second carriage, raise your hand!», «Third carriage, jump!», «Last carriage, say choo-choo!» Then swap places and play again!
t.s1b710c2a84: Well done! The tortoise is last.
t.s40f783ee57: In the line 🧒👧👦. What place is the one in the middle?
t.s1887a2ec82: Great job! The one in the middle is second.
t.sf198a79cd3: You're last in the line 🐢. How many children are behind you?
t.sefe0d42995: Super! There's nobody after the last one.
t.s56334a0ec5: Beep-beep! My friend, you've learned so many things! Soon the school doors will open for you. One last test: counting, sums and word problems. Are you ready? I believe in you!
t.se84374c195: A counting master counts to twenty forwards and backwards without mistakes and knows every number's neighbours. The neighbours of 15 are 14 and 16. You're a master too!
t.s837c7b5372: A sums master quickly adds and takes away within ten: counts on from the bigger number and remembers the friends of ten. 6 + 4 = 10, 10 − 4 = 6. Adding and taking away are brothers!
t.s2be8997aa3: Pretend to put your school bag on your shoulders!
t.se1e08abfbd: In our school bag there's a squared notebook, a pencil and a ruler 🎒. We can count, do sums, solve problems and tell the time. Now let's march bravely to school! Beep-beep! I'm proud of you!
t.s6a34690849: «I can count to twenty, plus and minus too, I tell time by the clock, and problems I can do — off to school I go!» Sing the song, put your bag on and march around the room like a champion! Beep-beep! Well done!
t.sa47b788073: Well done! They are friends of ten.
